summary.text: 有 means “exist” and “have; possess.” One analysis of bronze forms sees a hand holding meat, a scene associated with possession. Reported oracle-bone uses are read as “exist,” but neither settles the earliest meaning or structure.

formation.text: The construction is disputed. One analysis reads bronze forms as 又 (a hand) plus 肉, depicting a hand holding meat and associating the scene with possession. The received 說文 account instead analyzes 月 plus sound-bearing 又 and links 月 to eclipses. Neither account establishes the structure of every early form or that possession was the earliest meaning.

components.text: In the bronze-form analysis, 又 depicts the hand in the proposed hand-holding-meat scene and is also proposed as a sound element. Baxter–Sagart 2014 reconstructs 有 and 又 with a shared base and a suffix difference, a comparison that makes the sound analysis plausible without establishing the graph’s formation history.

sound_limitation.text: The available reconstructions support a plausible sound analysis but do not establish that 又 occurred in every early form or when and how the graph was formed.

components.text: In the bronze-form analysis, 肉 is the meat held by the hand and contributes to the proposed scene associated with possession. Its relation to the graph described in the received 說文 analysis is unresolved.

history.text: The received 說文 account analyzes 有 as 月 plus sound-bearing 又, cites 日月有食之, and links the word to something inauspicious that occurs. This is a transmitted interpretation of the graph and its use.

A separate analysis reads bronze forms as 又 plus 肉, depicting a hand holding meat. The selected seal-style illustration represents the received 說文 tradition; it is a modern digital reconstruction, not an ancient artifact image.

uncertainties.text: The proposed path from existence to possession is a scholarly interpretation: reported oracle-bone examples are read as existential, while a bronze inscription is cited for possession, but the examples do not establish a dated sequence.
The exact earliest attestation and the structures of particular early forms remain unresolved; whether they visibly contain 肉 is not settled by the available graphic accounts.

Proposed relationships to 侑 and 醢 and a whole-graph borrowing from the name of a depicted object are not substantiated here. A separate proposal reads a bronze form 㞢 as a bovine head on a board in a ritual; it is not established as the origin or meaning of 有.

senses.text: Reported oracle-bone uses, including 有虎? 亡其鹿?, are interpreted as existential. Their exact date and priority over every other early use are unresolved.
A bronze inscription is cited for possession, though the vessel’s date is unresolved here.

senses.text: The received 說文 discussion cites 有 in 日月有食之 and interprets the passage as something that should not occur but does.
The supplied definition records the current senses “have,” “own,” “possess,” and “exist.”

developments.text: One scholarly analysis argues that possession developed from existence, since possession presupposes existence; the cited examples do not establish a dated, stepwise transition.

limitations.text: The bronze possession example is not precisely dated, so it cannot date the proposed development from existence to possession.
The available examples do not establish a complete chronology for the senses “exist,” “have,” and “occur.”
